item.title: China issues first AI-plus-brain-computer interface medical-device standard
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: China’s National Medical Products Administration has approved YY/T 2029–2026, a medical-device industry standard covering EEG dataset quality requirements and evaluation methods for artificial-intelligence algorithms used in brain-computer interface devices. The standard covers data collection, processing, labeling, storage and access, and is intended to provide a consistent quality baseline for research, manufacturing, testing and regulation. It […]
item.content:encoded:
China’s National Medical Products Administration has approved YY/T 2029–2026, a medical-device industry standard covering EEG dataset quality requirements and evaluation methods for artificial-intelligence algorithms used in brain-computer interface devices.

The standard covers data collection, processing, labeling, storage and access, and is intended to provide a consistent quality baseline for research, manufacturing, testing and regulation. It is scheduled to take effect on Sept. 1, 2027. [China Food and Drug News, in Chinese]

item.content:encoded:
Xi’an Jiaotong University technology-transfer company Blue Insect Embodied has launched its modular Mantis Standard humanoid robot, also known as “Xiaobai,” at a starting price of RMB 9,800.

The robot’s chassis, arms, waist and head use standardized modules connected through quick-install interfaces. It has 22 degrees of freedom, a 7-kilogram single-arm payload, a 663-millimeter arm span and teleoperation latency below 10 milliseconds. Its waist can lift through 550 millimeters, while the omnidirectional base supports three degrees of freedom, a 3-meter-per-second forward speed and three hours of battery life. [Phoenix, in Chinese]

item.content:encoded:
Huawei and Seres will reportedly adjust their smart-car partnership this week, with Huawei moving to an asset-light model, according to people familiar with the matter.

The change would shift responsibility for products, marketing, sales and services from Huawei-led operations to a Seres-led model supported by Huawei. Hongmeng Zhixing will focus its resources on helping the Zhijie, Xiangjie, Zunjie and Shangjie brands succeed. [CLS, in Chinese]

item.content:encoded:
Dreame reportedly saw around 10,000 employees leave or lose their jobs between June and the end of August, according to the WeChat account Zhiwei. Compensation reportedly ranged from 0.5N for probationary employees to N+1.

The report said Dreame’s automotive and smartphone teams now have few employees left. Its AI smart-lock business unit was reportedly eliminated, while most of its home-appliance research and development team was cut, with sales, supply-chain and selected middle-office roles retained. [Zhiwei, in Chinese]

item.title: Unitree launches upgraded G1+ humanoid robot with six major upgrades
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Unitree has launched the G1+, an upgraded version of its G1 humanoid robot with six upgrades spanning motion performance, perception, interaction and endurance. The standard model is priced at RMB 95,000 in China, while the G1+ EDU version is available by contacting sales. The G1+ adds two neck degrees of freedom, raises peak shoulder-and-waist motor […]
item.content:encoded:
Unitree has launched the G1+, an upgraded version of its G1 humanoid robot with six upgrades spanning motion performance, perception, interaction and endurance. The standard model is priced at RMB 95,000 in China, while the G1+ EDU version is available by contacting sales.

The G1+ adds two neck degrees of freedom, raises peak shoulder-and-waist motor torque by 110% and maximum arm torque by 43%, and reduces heat at the same torque. It also adds a binocular-plus-wide-angle vision system, head touch sensing, external power support, a six-microphone array and dual 10-watt speakers. [Unitree]

ADrive is described as supporting natural-language and image search, document summaries, rewriting, translation, multi-document Q&A, file conversion […]
item.content:encoded:
ByteDance is reportedly preparing to launch a standalone intelligent cloud drive called ADrive in September. Built by Volcano Engine, the enterprise product is designed for collaboration between AI agents and human users, and trial applications are reportedly open.

ADrive is described as supporting natural-language and image search, document summaries, rewriting, translation, multi-document Q&A, file conversion and OCR. It also offers password-protected sharing, expiration settings, internal and external network access controls, and activity logs. [TechNode reporting]

The report cited an unnamed source quoted by Kechuangban Daily. Huawei launched the Pura X Max in April as a wide-format foldable […]
item.content:encoded:
Huawei’s Pura X Max foldable phone reportedly saw sales rise 76.5% from Sept. 10 to Sept. 13 compared with the same period a week earlier, after Apple launched its first foldable iPhone Duo. The report cited an unnamed source quoted by Kechuangban Daily.

Huawei launched the Pura X Max in April as a wide-format foldable phone starting at RMB 10,999. It has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.7-inch inner display, and uses Huawei’s Kirin 9030 Pro chip. [TechNode reporting]

item.title: Uzbekistan’s Tech Gambit: Nation Vies for Global Stage with New “Enterprise Uzbekistan” Free Zone
item.dc:creator: TechNode Staff
item.description: Uzbekistan is trying to position itself as a technology hub for Central Asia, combining tax incentives, sector-specific tech parks, a young workforce and closer regional ties. A key part of that push is “Enterprise Uzbekistan,” a free zone for technology companies and financial organizations that is expected to operate under English common law. Seven years […]
item.content:encoded:
Uzbekistan is trying to position itself as a technology hub for Central Asia, combining tax incentives, sector-specific tech parks, a young workforce and closer regional ties. A key part of that push is “Enterprise Uzbekistan,” a free zone for technology companies and financial organizations that is expected to operate under English common law.

Seven years after its launch, IT Park Uzbekistan has become a central part of the country’s digital strategy. Since its founding, Uzbekistan has seen a 13-fold increase in foreign direct investment inflows and a tripling of foreign trade turnover. StartupBlink recently ranked Uzbekistan as the world’s fastest-growing startup ecosystem.

A New Legal Framework for Tech and Investment

Enterprise Uzbekistan is designed to give foreign companies a legal environment separate from the domestic Uzbek system. Companies registered there would operate under English common law, a structure familiar to international investors and venture funds.

The zone is scheduled for a full launch in early 2027 and is modeled on international financial centers such as Astana and Dubai. It is expected to support structures such as limited partnerships and general partnerships, which are widely used in venture capital. The planned territory in Tashkent will exceed 10 hectares, and companies will be able to establish branches or holding structures under the regime.

Uzbekistan is also building specialized technoparks. IT Park focuses on software, digital products and IT exports; Inno Technopark on hardware and manufacturing; Creative Park on gaming, user-generated content and digital art; and Cyber Park on cybersecurity.

IT Park residents receive a 0% corporate tax, 0% social tax and a 7.5% personal income tax rate for employees. Foreign investors can own 100% of a company, registration can take as little as three working days, and the “Zero Risk” package offers a free office and equipment for one year to companies operating outside Tashkent.

Talent, Regions and the Startup Ecosystem

Uzbekistan also points to demographics as an advantage. About 65% of its 39 million people are under 35, and 146 universities offer IT-focused programs.

“We’re the number one English-speaking nation in Central Asia,” said Gul Hassan of IT Park’s partnership team during a presentation on September 10, 2026. He said younger people are increasingly adopting English over Russian as the country tries to integrate its workforce into the global digital economy.

Officials also highlight regional specializations. Fergana Valley is presented as a source of young talent and lower operating costs; Karakalpakstan as a potential hub for AI and data centers because of low water and electricity costs; and Bukhara and Samarkand as sources of talent in mathematics, physics and chemistry.

The startup market has expanded quickly. Uzbek startups raised $3 million in 2022, $329 million in 2025. The number of local venture funds has grown from two in 2022 to 22, with more than $200 million available for investment.

Government programs include Digital Uprise, which can match up to $100,000 in foreign venture capital invested in local startups, and the upcoming “President of Uzbekistan’s Land of Startups” competition, with a $5 million prize fund.

Regional Collaboration and the Next Step

Uzbekistan is also working more closely with Kazakhstan’s Astana Hub, promoting the region under initiatives such as the “Central Asian Innovation Hub.” Tajikistan has joined the effort, and Azerbaijan is expected to participate as well.

When comparing Uzbekistan with Kazakhstan, one official emphasized market size while acknowledging Kazakhstan’s head start: “If you’re looking for a market, Uzbekistan is the better one because we are like a half Central Asian population.”

Uzbekistan’s strategy combines legal reform, tax incentives, talent development and regional cooperation. The launch of Enterprise Uzbekistan could add another tool for attracting international technology companies and investors.

Questions remain over whether infrastructure outside Tashkent can keep pace with high-tech industries and whether the workforce can scale fast enough. For now, Uzbekistan is betting that digital services, startups and stronger links with global capital can drive its next stage of growth.

MTR Lab and Northern Light Venture Capital co-led the round, with Voyagers Partners acting as financial adviser. The company plans to use the funds to expand enterprise security governance infrastructure for the […]
item.content:encoded:
Eagle Cloud has closed a Series B+ funding round of nearly RMB 100 million (about $14 million), four months after its Series B. MTR Lab and Northern Light Venture Capital co-led the round, with Voyagers Partners acting as financial adviser.

The company plans to use the funds to expand enterprise security governance infrastructure for the AI agent era and accelerate overseas expansion. Its Yunshu platform includes AIDR (AI Detection & Response), which covers AI discovery, definition, identification, enforcement and measurement across the lifecycle. [TechNode reporting]

item.title: Baidu to rename Baijiahao app as Baidu Live Companion on Sept. 22
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Baidu will rename its Baijiahao app as Baidu Live Companion on Sept. 22, shifting the app’s focus toward livestreaming. User accounts, historical content and accumulated earnings will remain unchanged. Non-livestream creators will continue managing their work through the creation center in the Baidu app, while livestream creators can use the renamed app. [17173, in Chinese]
